title: Manchurian plague and Wu Lien-teh's response
summary: A pneumonic plague outbreak that began at Manzhouli in October 1910 spread to Harbin and other Manchurian cities, with an estimated 60,000 or more deaths. The Cambridge-trained physician Wu Lien-teh was sent to lead the response in December 1910, backed mass cremation from 31 January 1911, and presided at the international conference at Mukden in April 1911. The last case was recorded on 1 March 1911.

uncertainty.note: Outbreak October 1910 (Harbin cases identified 27 October 1910); epidemic declared over by end of April 1911; last recorded case 1 March 1911.

where.historical_name: Harbin and Fuchiatien (Fujiadian), Manchuria, Qing China

importance.justification: A major pneumonic plague epidemic whose control is credited to measures that shaped modern public health in China.

audience_note: Describes a deadly epidemic with mass deaths and the cremation of thousands of unburied bodies.
